analysis: The code snippet contains two calls to `substring`: `line.substring(0, commentDelim)` and `line.substring(0, delim)` and `line.substring(delim)`. The first call is guarded by `if (commentDelim >= 0)`, which ensures `commentDelim` is non-negative. Since `indexOf('#')` returns -1 only when '#' is absent, the guard prevents the case where `commentDelim` is -1 (which would cause beginIndex > endIndex). Similarly, the second set of calls is guarded by `if (delim >= 0)`, ensuring `delim` is non-negative. Since `indexOf(' ')` returns -1 only when no space is present, the guard prevents negative indices. Additionally, `indexOf` returns values within the string length (0 to length-1), so both beginIndex (0) and endIndex (commentDelim or delim) are within valid bounds. Thus, the throwing conditions for `IndexOutOfBoundsException` (negative index or index larger than length) are fully avoided.
